medSchoolStudLife.diversity: WashU is committed to the recruitment, selection, education, retention, and graduation of students with multiple perspectives and experiences. Students are supported by active chapters of multiple organizations, student interest groups, and a diverse network of residents and faculty.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A student may request a leave of absence for academic or personal reasons by submitting a statement in writing to the Dean of Student Affairs.  The statement should indicate the beginning and anticipated ending dates and should briefly state the reason for the request.  Requests for up to a one year's leave of absence my be approved by the Associate Dean for Student Affairs.  Leaves extending beyond one year shall require the review and approval of the Committee on the Academic and Professional Evaluation of Students (CAPES).  In rare instances, more extended leaves may be approved if the student seeks to complete a degree program requiring two or more years.  Students requiring a leave of absence for medical reasons must submit a supporting letter from the Director of the Student Health Service.  A written statement of medical clearance will be required before the student may return from a medical leave.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: At WashU Medicine, it is paramount that students not just ‘survive’, but thrive in medical school. More than 100 student-initiated, student-run organizations fulfill our students' endless drive to contribute to their community as well as to develop interests outside of the curriculum. WashU Medicine enthusiastically supports student co-curricular engagement, whether related to medicine or to creative endeavors such as music, writing, and fitness. These groups provide fabulous opportunities to make a difference in the community, have fun, and find mentorship. Current groups involve the arts, service and support activities, medical specialty interests, government and political activities, medical entrepreneurship, and social activities promoting wellness, social support, and personal growth. See https://mdadmissions.wustl.edu/student-life/student-run-groups/.
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
The WashU Medicine is located in the city's Central West End ( https://mdadmissions.wustl.edu/student-life/st-louis/the-central-west-end/ ), an eclectic neighborhood that is a favorite among students. The WashU medical campus consists of 186 acres, spread over 18 city blocks. Forest Park ( https://mdadmissions.wustl.edu/student-life/st-louis/forest-park/ ) is a wonderful natural resource adjacent to campus, providing over 1300 acres of greenspace and numerous recreational options. The Cortex Innovation Community neighbors the campus on the east. See https://mdadmissions.wustl.edu/facts-and-resources/about-the-medical-campus/.

Saint Louis has been nicknamed the “Gateway to the West” and is a thriving metropolitan area of 2.8 million people that retains the friendly character of the Midwest. The fun and culture of a big city are readily available, but living here is easy and affordable. See https://mdadmissions.wustl.edu/student-life/st-louis/ and https://explorestlouis.com/
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
St. Louis is nationally recognized for its abundant, convenient, safe, and affordable housing. In August 2018, the Core Apartment Residences opened adjacent to the medical campus. See https://mdadmissions.wustl.edu/student-life/housing/ for more information on this on-campus housing option as well as for resources for off-campus housing, including Washington University-affiliate Quadrangle Housing.  

Our first-year medical students' comments regarding housing are updated annually in our "Dis-Orientation Guide", a student-written publication, with sections on neighborhoods, apartment complexes, and virtual tours. See the Dis-O "Housing" tab at https://mdadmissions.wustl.edu/student-life/dis-o-guide/.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Students identifying as a gender or sexual minority have access to LGBTQ Med, a student-run interest group dedicated to lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer (LGBTQ+) identity and health. Additionally, students have access to OUTmed, an organization for LGBTQIA-identified faculty, residents, fellows and staff at WashUMedicine. OUTmed fosters networking and mentoring relationships for LGBTQIA students, faculty, residents and staff.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Our students are encouraged to connect with the Office of Disability Resources, which provides support and accommodations for students with disabilities to ensure accessible learning experiences. You can learn more at https://md.wustl.edu/academic-support/ and https://disability.washu.edu/.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Our students' overall health and wellness is of paramount importance to us. The Office of Medical Student Affairs, other WashU Medicine offices, and medical students themselves provide a number of services and opportunities to help you maintain wellness in all aspects of your life. In addition to the school’s academic, financial, mental, physical, social and spiritual wellness resources, there are many student-led entities that promote and organize events fostering student wellness, namely the Society Coordinators and Social Chairs. You can learn more at https://md.wustl.edu/resources/wellness/.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: At WashU Medicine future medical leaders work alongside the greatest minds in medicine, playing a vital role in the future of healthcare. Mission-driven students select WashU Medicine for the culture of collaboration and support, flexible curriculum and outstanding opportunities after graduation.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo:
More information regarding the transportation policy is available at https://bulletin.wustl.edu/medicine/policies/md-transportation/.

The city's Metrolink light rail and bus transportation systems are free to students. A light rail stop and a bus transit center are both centrally located on the WashU Medicine Campus and WashU Danforth Campus.

medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Variable. Active learning pedagogies are emphasized (e.g., small group discussion, team-based learning; one-on-one with faculty);  online learning management system, reading electives, and lecture.

medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: Through the Gateway Curriculum we are advancing human health and inspiring learners to create the future in medicine, science, and society. We will produce physicians who are leaders in medicine - leaders in clinical care, science, education, and advocacy. The Gateway Curriculum is a competency-based and outcomes-oriented approach to medical education, centered around the learner, integrating classroom and clinical learning in a manner that is sustainable for the changing landscape of medicine. The Gateway Curriculum consists of three phases over four calendar years. Throughout the three phases, students participate in the EXPLORE Curriculum, which provides students with longitudinal and immersive experiences in four specific academic career pathways: Research, Education, Advocacy/Global Health, and Innovation. Dual degree programs including MD/MBA, MD/MPH, MD/MPHS, MD/MSBDS-AI, MD/MSCI, and MD/PhD are available for students desiring further training.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
All students participate in a three-week clinical immersion, where they work with preceptors in Ambulatory (primarily Primary Care) and Emergency Department care settings during Phase 1.

During Phase 3, students have the opportunity to participate in a rigorous Primary Care Advanced Clinical Rotation based in ambulatory clinics. They also have the option to take an elective in Family Medicine.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
Students have full access to WashU's research enterprise, which is among the most extensive in the world. Discovery happens across the full spectrum of research, from fundamental basic science to clinical and translational investigation. Students have the opportunity to learn fundamental concepts of research, and to work with passionate and dedicated research mentors.  For more information about medical student research, please visit https://md.wustl.edu/career-development/explore/research-pathway/

There are many training opportunities available for those who aspire to develop themselves as physician scientists and clinical researchers. One option is the school's MD/PhD medical scientist training program--one of the largest in the country. A second option is to participate in the Yearlong Research Program after second or third year. A third option is to schedule research electives in Phase 3, up to 10 months in total duration.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: WashU Medicine is located in the historic, culturally diverse, and affordable Central West End neighborhood. Dedicated solely to medical education and located at the heart of the 186-acre urban medical campus, the Farrell Learning and Teaching Center provides a state-of-the-art facility in which to learn the compassionate delivery of scientific medicine. This facility complements outstanding clinical resources at Barnes-Jewish Hospital and St. Louis Children's Hospital, two of the top academic hospitals in the country. Learning among the most talented classmates in the country and in world-class facilities, medical students at WashU enjoy a supportive and noncompetitive environment where opportunities for discovery, learning and self-fulfillment abound.  With more than 26,000 employees, the combined Medical Campus institutions are among the largest employers in the St. Louis metropolitan area generating an annual economic impact of over $7.5 billion for the St. Louis region.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
In leading the advancement of human health, WashU Medicine will:
Cultivate excellence and collegiality within an equitable and inclusive community.
Attract, develop, advance and support a diverse and talented current and future workforce.
Innovate through discoveries and inventions in basic, clinical, translational and population sciences.
Build and support an environment that fosters exceptionally creative research, health care, education and the well-being of our workforce.
Use our academic excellence and scientific rigor to continually advance and enhance health care in a way that ensures access, compassion, high value, equity and evidence-based care for all people in our community, including those who are underserved and uninsured.
Observe the highest standards of ethics, integrity and humanity across all of our missions.
Apply advances in research, education and health care for the betterment of the human condition, locally and globally.

Educating tomorrow’s leaders in biomedicine involved reimagining a medical curriculum that fosters both self-directed and team-based learning.  The Gateway Curriculum, implemented in 2020, provides exposure to research and advocacy in basic science, clinical-translational science, public and population health, primary care, and the social sciences, as well as longitudinal experiences with patients in community-based settings. Such a dynamic curriculum enables students to create new science that will enrich the health of our community, while becoming empathic practitioners who will commit to eliminating intractable and unconscionable health disparities. Our Gateway Curriculum ensures that our students are not only exceptional physicians, but that they understand the social and structural determinants of health and are prepared to lead transformational changes needed to improve our future.  The EXPLORE program within Gateway is a formalized approach to career development that helps students find their niche in academic medicine among four pathways: Advocacy/Global Health, Education, Innovation, and Research. 

A network of faculty coaches facilitates students’ navigation through the curriculum and ensures that our students are reaching their full personal and professional potential.  The Career Counseling Office works closely with students to explore the possibilities for graduate medical training and careers.

Our Office of Admissions operates under a mission-aligned framework.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
Letters must be received by October 29, 2026.  Letters should be on letterhead, dated and signed.  

Letters should provide an in-depth evaluation of the applicant's accomplishments, skills, talents and character, rather than a mere recapitulation of academic achievement or course grade(s). Washington University supports the movement for letters to cover AAMC's Core Competencies for Entering Medical Students, and encourages applicants to solicit letters from individuals who can address these competencies.

Additional Letters: If a committee letter or letter packet is being submitted for you, up to three additional individual letters may also be submitted on your behalf.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
In general, we require three letters of evaluation, which may be submitted individually or collected for submission by a prior or current educational institution (“letter packet”). Typically, letters should come from at least one or two instructors at a college or university who know the applicant well enough to write on their behalf. Letters may also come from research mentors, extracurricular or postgraduate advisors, mentors or supervisors. 

If you are pursuing or have an advanced degree or at least one year of postgraduate full-time employment, it is advisable to ask a member of your graduate faculty or your work supervisor to send a letter of evaluation.

Applicants are permitted to submit a letter prepared by a premedical advisor or committee, either in addition to individual letters, or as a substitute for them if this is the typical practice at their school. The submission of either a committee letter or letter packet fulfills the letter of evaluation requirement.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Information for 2027 Admissions Cycle

Pass/Fail Courses, Online Coursework and Labs:
Courses used to meet prerequisites must appear on a transcript; WashU Medicine will only accept credits earned at an institution accredited by one of the seven regional Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) bodies in the United States, institutions recognized by Universities Canada, or an American College Overseas, as defined in the AMCAS Applicant Guide. The COA will consider the rigor of the applicant’s curriculum, their performance in each class, and grading practices at their institution. We do accept courses that have been taken pass/fail. We also accept courses taken at a community college, through a summer school or utilizing an online method of instruction. Prerequisites may be met in this manner. However, the majority of classes, especially science classes, should optimally be taken for a letter grade at an individual’s primary undergraduate institution.

Find more information on https://mdadmissions.wustl.edu/how-to-apply/requirements/

As a participant in the American Medical College Application Service® (AMCAS®), WashU Medicine abides by the Application and Acceptance Protocols established by the AAMC and encourages students to use the accompanying AMCAS® Choose Your Medical School Tool. Applicants holding at least one acceptance from any medical school will have the option to “Plan to Enroll” in mid-February. 

Per WashU Medicine Admissions policy, applicants who have been offered admission to WashU Medicine and intend to matriculate at WashU Medicine should indicate they “Plan to Enroll” through the Choose Your Medical School Tool as soon as possible, but no later than April 30 of the year in which they will matriculate. WashU Medicine reserves the right to rescind offers of acceptance if an applicant has not selected “Plan to Enroll” by April 30. After April 30, while an applicant maintains the “Plan to Enroll” status at WashU Medicine, applicants may continue to hold positions on the waitlist of other schools.

Beginning April 30, accepted applicants have the option to “Commit to Enroll” (CTE) at WashU Medicine. When an applicant selects “CTE” to WashU Medicine, they should notify all other institutions where they hold an acceptance or position on the waitlist that they wish to withdraw their acceptance or position on the waitlist from that school. WashU Medicine reserves the right to rescind an offer of admission to any applicant still holding an active acceptance at another institution while having a “CTE” status with WashU Medicine. WashU Medicine reserves the right to rescind offers of admission from any applicant still holding a WashU Medicine acceptance while indicating that they either “Plan to Enroll” or “Commit to Enroll” at another institution after April 30.   

For applicants accepted after April 30, the timeline for selecting “Plan to Enroll” will be specified by the Associate Dean for Admissions.

All MSTP applicants planning to matriculate at WashU Medicine should select the "CTE" option no later than May 30, 2027.
All MD applicants planning to matriculate at WashU Medicine should select the "CTE" option no later than July 20, 2027.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: WashU Medicine follows the mission-aligned selection process recommended by the AAMC in assessing applicants’ capabilities. Mission-aligned selection is a flexible, mission-driven approach to recruit and assess an individual’s competencies by considering their experiences, attributes, and academic metrics in order to select applicants who will best contribute to the program’s unique goals, learning environment, and the practice of medicine.

medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We accept courses taken at a community college, through a summer school or online, as long as the institution meets our accreditation requirements. medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo:
Updates - We welcome updates once your AMCAS application has been verified and will add them to your application file for review and consideration by our Committee on Admissions. We ask that you limit your updates to those that are significant and relevant to your application.

Letters of Interest - We welcome letters of interest at any time during the admissions cycle and will add them to your application file for review and consideration by our Committee on Admissions.

Letters of Intent - We welcome letters of intent after an applicant has interviewed and will add them to your application file for review and consideration by our Committee on Admissions.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
To effectively engage in all aspects of the curriculum, individuals pursuing a Doctor of Medicine degree at WashU Medicine are expected to meet our Technical Standards, either with or without reasonable accommodations. Technical Standards are the skills, abilities, attributes, and characteristics that WashU Medicine deems essential for achieving competency in the practice of medicine, as outlined in the school’s medical education program objectives.

The ability to meet WashU Medicine Technical Standards is a requirement for admission and, along with the attainment of the medical education program objectives, for promotion and graduation. Upon application, matriculation, and at the start of each phase of the curriculum, students must attest that they can meet WashU Medicine Technical Standards with or without reasonable accommodations. This attestation also offers students a formal opportunity to proactively seek support in meeting the evolving demands of their education.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The financial resources of an applicant do not enter into the selection process for admissions. Tuition is set at entry and does not increase during the four years of medical school. A required student health fee and other expenses such as books, medical supplies, food and rent will change annually. Merit-based scholarships are awarded by the Office of Admissions to selected students in each entering class and are renewable each year. Accepted U.S. citizens and permanent residents who apply for need-based financial aid may qualify and receive such financial aid, comprised of both scholarships and loans. Awarded need-based loans, federal and/or institutional, are currently capped at 35% of the cost of attendance. Need-based scholarships and institutional loans awarded upon entry are locked in for future years. Students who borrow via federal loans must re-apply annually. Accepted students who are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents are required to provide proof of funding for all four years of the MD curriculum, including tuition, fees, and living expenses, in the form of an escrow or letter of credit prior to matriculation.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Tuition is locked for five years, additional time is considered via an appeal process

medSchoolPrograms.info:
The MD/MSBDS-AI is not a joint acceptance program, rather MD students apply to this program as third-year students.  The interdisciplinary MS and certificate programs in Biomedical Data Science & AI (BDS-AI) provide students with a competency-based training in core biomedical data science, biostatistics, and informatics theories and methods to address the fundamental shift health and life sciences are experiencing toward transdisciplinary, integrative and data-intensive approaches to research. The MSBDS-AI offers three distinct concentrations, allowing students to tailor their training to align with their interests and career goals. After completing a shared first semester of foundational coursework, students select one of the following tracks to dive deeper into advanced topics: Biostatistics, Biomedical informatics, or Data Science.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Required course work: A minimum of one year (two semesters) or equivalent advanced placement in:
Biological science
General or inorganic chemistry
Organic chemistry*
Physics
Calculus**

Laboratories in the sciences are recommended but not required.
Possible substitutions:
* One semester of biochemistry can be substituted for one semester of organic chemistry. A course in biochemistry, though not required, is encouraged.
** Statistics or biostatistics can be substituted for one semester of calculus. 

In selected instances, one or more of these prerequisites may be waived by the Committee on Admissions.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Although there is no expiration date for when prerequisite coursework can be completed, it is recommended that applicants have recent experience in these courses.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: A good doctor must be compassionate and understanding, as well as a good scientist. To this end, WashU Medicine selects students who, in addition to possessing keen minds, demonstrate sensitivity and a commitment to serve others. Hence, students are selected on the basis of character, attitude, interest, intellectual ability, motivation, maturity, and achievement as indicated by superior academic and extracurricular accomplishments. Policies and programs are nondiscriminatory, and full consideration is given to all applicants without regard to race, color, age, sex, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national or ethnic origin, veteran status, disability, or genetic information. Selected applicants are invited to interview, which is required for acceptance.
